title: Qwen38-27B adaptive KV streaming

checkpoints.title: Raymond Huang adaptive streaming and phase arena
Speculative streaming: local changes based on this commit; per-case source hashes are recorded

notes: Streaming sweeps use 262144 context. The separately requested original-executable comparison uses its launcher settings: native KV, 110000 context, batch 1024, microbatch 512. All keep Q8 KV and the CPU projector.
Screening requests are shorter than the requested 150000-token full generation. They are labeled separately.
The sweep input is exactly 2000 token IDs; additional prefill diagnostics use 61520. EOS is ignored; throughput is not a text-quality evaluation.
GPU peaks are total-device samples every two seconds, including background applications.
New speculative runs also sample GPU temperature, clocks, power and clock-event flags. They stop at 85 C or an active thermal slowdown flag; CPU temperature is not monitored.
Intentional host KV and CPU projector allocations are not VRAM spill.
The streaming guard stops after three free-VRAM samples below 192 MiB. One explicitly monitored original-110K retry used 64 MiB. These pressure guards do not prove WDDM paging.
The original-executable 64K comparison was requested to restore headroom; it is separate from the 262144-context streaming sweep.
Cold and warm mean first and subsequent requests. Startup warmup does not remove all first-request overhead. Every measured request requires zero reused prompt tokens.
Disabling context checkpoints can improve prefill but can require more recomputation when reusing an earlier prompt prefix. Checkpoint count is recorded per configuration.
The original sweep deferred speculation. Later DFlash2/MTP variants use the local verification-arena implementation; draft caches remain separate from the streamed target cache.

findings: Stopped at the user request after 142422 generated tokens, with 2000 input tokens. The 150000-token target was not completed.
Warm 2K prefill met the target: 1875 t/s in the sustained run and 1878 t/s mean across three tuning repeats. The original executable at 64K measured 1814 t/s on its warm 2K request.
Microbatch 1024, batch 2048, a 3750 MiB arena and zero context checkpoints were selected. The multimodal projector remained on CPU; target K and V stayed Q8_0 at 262144 context capacity.
Decode began near 53 t/s and was about 35 t/s near 100K generated tokens. It dropped sharply after total context exceeded the approximately 112384-token resident KV prefix.
The first measured interval below 13 t/s ended at 117761 generated tokens (119761 total context). The last full interval was 4.58 t/s; the final partial interval was about 4.4 t/s.
Peak total-device GPU use was 15556 MiB, minimum free GPU memory 421 MiB, and peak process RAM about 21.21 GiB. No free-VRAM guard fired. These counters do not prove that WDDM never paged memory.

This configuration achieves the prefill goal and contains GPU memory use, but does not sustain 13 t/s decode at roughly 144K populated context. A 262K capacity setting is not evidence of fast full-capacity inference.
Normal startup warmup was insufficient to remove the first-request penalty. Use a representative warmup request and measure subsequent uncached requests separately.

Zero context checkpoints reduces prefill overhead but can require more recomputation when returning to an earlier prompt prefix. Speculative decoding was deferred; no MTP or DFlash2 benchmark was completed.

Only one sustained run of the final configuration was measured. Short screens, original-executable diagnostics, repeats, and the earlier interrupted run remain separate; generation quality was not evaluated.

Follow-up diagnosis: measured pinned host-to-GPU bandwidth was 7.21 GB/s, with PCIe Gen 3 x8 confirmed under copy load. Raymond reports about 50 GB/s and uses Q8 K / Q4 V on Linux. Our Q8/Q8 Windows measurements are not a matched comparison.

The final logged adaptive partition was 431 resident pages per layer and 149 ring slots, demonstrating active adaptation. Estimated streamed KV near the endpoint is 1.19 GB per token, implying about 6.1 t/s as a transfer-only upper bound at the measured bandwidth. This supports a bandwidth bottleneck but does not rule out a software regression; actual KV transfer traffic was not instrumented.

speculative_validation.title: Speculative streaming validation
limitations: These 16K-context checks intentionally force streaming with a 320 MiB arena. They are separate from the 262K performance sweep.
Native and streamed model outputs are not bit-identical. Prefix logprob differences are recorded; CUDA references test attention numerically.
Prefix reuse continues each variant's own accepted output, so reuse requests are not cross-variant output comparisons.
Qwen4Exp speculative validation is limited to CUDA attention tests; no compatible drafter model was available.
The final context change bounds decode reservation to 32 queries and uses the prefill layout for larger batches. It does not change these three-draft-token checks.
